title: Experimental and theoretical determination of vapor pressures of NaCl-KCl, NaBr-KBr and NaCl-CaCl2 aqueous solutions at 298 to 343 K
experimental_method: Static method with an isoteniscope and U-tube null indicator in a windowed thermostat; absolute pressure read with an MKS Baratron transducer; solutions degassed by boiling and freezing; 298.15-343.15 K in 5 K steps.
uncertainties_stated: Transducer relative accuracy 0.5%; temperature to 0.1 K; salt concentration standard deviation below 0.003 m (from triplicate samples); pure-water test: mean deviation 0.13% from literature, maximum below 0.5%; U-tube level difference <1 mm gives error within 0.074 torr.
quality_remarks: Salt concentration obtained from the weight fraction of the mixed salts made up beforehand (salt non-volatile). Salt purities: NaCl 99.95 mass%, CaCl2 97.5 mass% (Baker). Pressures given to 0.1 torr only. Table 2 (NaBr-KBr) has bromide salts and is out of scope.
